summary:
Chelyabinsk Oblast stands under the national framework of Russia. The UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025, assessment section updated 11 June 2025) sets out the conditions in force across every region of the country and records no region-specific findings for this oblast.

No law, enforcement action, institution, incident or protection measure specific to Chelyabinsk Oblast was identified in the sources available. The applicable law, penalties and enforcement practice for a visitor here are those set out in the national assessment of Russia; the material consulted for this region adds nothing to them.
tangentialFactors:
Comparisons between Chelyabinsk Oblast and other Russian regions cannot be drawn from the material available. The country policy and information note treats Russia as a single jurisdiction, and the enforcement figures it cites are national totals that the source does not disaggregate by region.

Because those national figures combine every region, no share of them can be attributed to Chelyabinsk Oblast, and the oblast cannot be ranked against any other region on this evidence.
localsOnly: No measure specific to residents of Chelyabinsk Oblast appears in the sources. Regional or municipal rules on documents, healthcare, facilities or protection for transgender residents are not documented in the material consulted, and residents here are subject to the national legal regime on the same terms as the rest of Russia.
outOfScopeNotes:
The source inventory for this region consists of one document that addresses Russia nationally and states that it offers no region-specific findings. National penalty levels, the November 2023 designation of the international LGBT+ movement as extremist and the count of persons affected by enforcement of anti-LGBT+ laws are national matters, set out in the assessment of Russia rather than here.

The national enforcement figures are totals with no regional breakdown, and the source presents them as floors rather than complete counts. No share of them can be attributed to Chelyabinsk Oblast, and no comparison with the general homicide or crime rate can be derived from them.
